prerequisites: good knowledge of the contents of Calculus I

learning_outcomes.text: Distinguish between the different interpretations of probability, and determine which is the most appropriate in each context.
Combine the probabilities of different events, and update them in light of new information.
Understand the concept of a random variable as a model of the outcome of an experiment under uncertainty, and the main characteristics of its probabilistic information.
Know the main models of probability distributions in the context of data analysis, distinguishing which is the most appropriate for each experiment.
Work with random vectors as a model for the simultaneous observation of several variables, handling with ease the main aspects of their probabilistic information.
Understand and handle the concept of reproducibility.
Know the main models of multivariate probability distributions.
Know the concept of stochastic process, and some of its applications in data analysis.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to probability. Interpretations: classical, frequentist, subjective.
Axiomatic definition of probability. Notable properties.
Probability distributions: density function, probability mass function and distribution function.
Parameters of a probability distribution: expectation, variance and moments. Characteristic function.
Discrete distributions: binomial, Poisson, negative binomial and hypergeometric.
Other continuous distributions: beta, gamma and other distributions derived from the normal.
Parameters of a multivariate distribution. Correlation.
Functions of multivariate variables and changes of variable.

assessment_methods.method: Final exam (written test with practical exercises and optional theoretical questions)
Active participation in forums and virtual campus activities (short exercises)

assessment_rules: The evaluation includes a final written exam (65%), attendance and tutorials (5%), active participation in forums and virtual campus activities (10%), and a laboratory practices exam (20%). There is no minimum score required in any single assessment element. For extraordinary calls, the evaluation system is the same, and grades from each section can be retained. Students with differentiated evaluation can choose between continuous assessment or a single final exam.
